discrepancy_taxonomy.B: project interpretation/specification incomplete or inconsistent with stronger Loihi evidence
discrepancy_taxonomy.C: Catalyst N1 makes a different architectural choice
discrepancy_taxonomy.D: Brian2Loihi makes or exposes a different modeling choice
discrepancy_taxonomy.E: published Loihi evidence is ambiguous or insufficient
discrepancy_taxonomy.G: feature is unsupported or outside the project's validated subset

accepted_agreements.finding: Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst RTL CUBA agree for the positive isolated-impulse current sequence after the frozen one-native-tick Catalyst staging transform.
Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst RTL CUBA agree for the positive isolated-impulse voltage sequence after the same frozen staging transform.
Strict project/Brian threshold behavior agrees with Catalyst after the predeclared Catalyst native-threshold transform T+1.
For canonical refractory duration R=3, all three executable software participants spike on ticks 0 and 3; raw refractory registers remain non-comparable.
After translating Catalyst compiler placement back to logical IDs, real Catalyst compiled fan-in produces 192 and fan-out produces target drives 64, 128, and 192, matching the common logical graph.
Project, Brian2Loihi, and Catalyst agree on the per-tick simultaneous spike set; global spike/event ordering remains non-comparable.

directed_adjudications.finding: Pinned Catalyst RTL CUBA uses a different negative /4096 rounding implementation from the project/Brian2Loihi rule.
Catalyst CPU simple-LIF returns sufficiently negative sub-rest drive to resting=0, while project/Brian2Loihi retain negative membrane state; the mixed net-positive case agrees.

All 13 of 15 project/Brian effective weights that fit Catalyst's signed-int16 compiler boundary are reproduced exactly by Catalyst. Catalyst does not expose the same Loihi-style source mantissa/exponent/precision/sign-mode encoding, and two project/Brian cases lie outside the common int16 envelope.

Same-source same-tick event multiplicity has no defensible common exact boundary: the project preserves repeated events, Brian SpikeGeneratorGroup cannot encode two spikes from one source at one time, and Catalyst external stimulus is not the same event-list interface.

Project and Catalyst synchronous recurrence deliver a one-tick source-to-target effect. Under Brian2Loihi 0.5.2's own LoihiNetwork schedule, the directed neuron-to-neuron recurrent connection produced no target effect; an independent diagnostic reproduced the null result for native synaptic delays 0, 1, and 2 over six ticks.

Finite-width overflow/saturation remains intentionally outside the common exact normalization because state widths and exposed probe widths differ and available published Loihi evidence does not justify one shared contract.

resolved_harness_findings.issue: The initial Catalyst CUBA negative probe reused a neuron whose SRAM state survived control reset.
resolved_harness_findings.resolution: Positive and negative probes now use independent neuron state slots; the negative native staging tick is current=-64, voltage=0.

resolved_harness_findings.issue: The initial Catalyst graph observer treated physical compiler GIDs as logical population IDs.
resolved_harness_findings.resolution: Native graph traces now preserve logical_to_catalyst_gid and remap potential, refractory state, and spike IDs back to logical order before comparison.

scope_and_comparison_findings.finding: FPGA-v1 intentionally excludes dendritic compartments, general programmable synaptic delays, native synapse-memory equivalence, inter-core routing/NoC, online learning, Loihi-like management processors, multicore scaling, and asynchronous/quiescence execution.
The pinned Catalyst K26-class source reproduces through routed implementation but does not supply the complete KV260 board integration needed for attributable physical execution.
M13.5 routed timing and resource totals are contextual only because target part strings, configured capacity, architectural scope, host/debug infrastructure, and execution evidence differ.

change_control.reason: No accepted M13 discrepancy is Class A or B. Classes C-G are retained as architectural, modeling, ambiguity, normalization, or scope findings; resolved Class-H issues affected only the audit harness.

qualified_project_catalyst_recurrent_sup.brian2loihi_result: no target effect observed at the pinned native probe boundary

claim_boundary.weight_common_envelope: 13 of 15 project/Brian2Loihi effective-weight cases fit Catalyst signed-int16 and agree exactly
not_claimed_as_universal_loihi_semantics: global ordering of coincident spike/event messages
same-source same-tick external event multiplicity across all backends
Catalyst negative CUBA rounding or sub-rest clamp behavior as Loihi ground truth
Brian2Loihi recurrent null behavior as Loihi ground truth
physical Catalyst KV260 execution from the pinned routed-only source boundary
performance or efficiency ranking from M13.5 raw resource/timing totals

experiment_handoff.guardrail: Treat altered update ordering as an explicit counterfactual; the validated FPGA-v1 schedule remains the baseline.
Catalyst native encoding is not field-for-field equivalent to the project/Brian2Loihi source encoding; compare delivered effective weight first.
Project and Catalyst synchronous recurrence support a one-tick lag; the Brian2Loihi null result is an emulator/modeling finding, not a Loihi ground-truth variant.
Alternative negative rounding, sub-rest clamping, and overflow policies are architecture counterfactuals unless stronger Loihi evidence establishes one as normative.
Do not combine architecture differences before isolated variants are independently validated.
Fair FPGA cost experiments should compare controlled project variants on the same target/tool boundary; raw Catalyst totals are contextual only.

closure_decision.next_gate: independent local reproduction of M13.6 source-level findings and full regression
